stories.headline: Carney downplays Pentagon defence spending critique as NATO commander offers praise
stories.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney stated that U.S. President Donald Trump has not brought up the Pentagon's critical assessment of Canadian defence spending during their bilateral conversations. The Pentagon recently issued a fact sheet arguing that Canada is failing to contribute its fair share toward continental and North American security. Meanwhile, NATO's deputy commander struck a contrasting and supportive tone, commending Canada's military rebuild efforts and its active contributions to European deterrence.

stories.headline: Supreme Court prepares landmark ruling on Quebec secularism law and Charter rights
stories.summary: The Supreme Court of Canada is poised to deliver a historic ruling on Quebec's Bill 21, which prohibits certain public sector employees from wearing religious symbols on the job. The decision could establish new limits on provincial use of the Charter's notwithstanding clause and dramatically alter federal-provincial relations. Observers across the country are watching closely as the ruling has the potential to reshape Canadian constitutional law and minority rights protections.

stories.headline: Senate committee amends federal lawful-access bill to strengthen cybersecurity safeguards
stories.summary: A Senate national security committee has adopted amendments to the federal government's controversial lawful-access legislation, Bill C-22, to address mounting concerns from tech companies and privacy advocates. The bill, which broadens police and intelligence agency access to digital subscriber information, was altered to clarify provisions and reinforce privacy protections against cyber vulnerabilities. While tech stakeholders welcomed the adjustments, several civil liberties and cybersecurity experts warned that the changes do not go far enough to prevent warrantless overreach.

stories.headline: Federal government defends expanded land expropriation powers for Alto high-speed rail
stories.summary: Transport Minister Steven MacKinnon defended federal plans to grant Ottawa broad authority to seize land along the proposed Alto high-speed rail corridor between Toronto and Quebec City, including transferring expropriated properties to private consortia. Opposition leaders condemned the measure as overbearing and authoritarian, with Bloc Québécois Leader Yves-François Blanchet accusing Prime Minister Mark Carney of acting like a pharaoh. Meanwhile, rail and transport researchers dismissed alternative route proposals from Quebec agricultural producers as technically unrealistic.

stories.headline: Study reveals deep income and racial disparities in access to family doctors
stories.summary: A new study by the Canadian Institute for Health Information found that adults living in lower-income neighbourhoods are significantly less likely to have a regular family doctor and more likely to be hospitalized for preventable conditions. The data also highlighted that Black and Latin American Canadians, young adults, and men face disproportionate barriers to securing primary care providers. Health researchers emphasized that persistent inequities in frontline care drive avoidable hospital admissions and worsen health outcomes.

stories.headline: Health Canada issues warning over rare vision loss risk from semaglutide medications
stories.summary: Health Canada has issued a public advisory regarding a very rare but serious risk of vision loss associated with GLP-1 receptor agonist medications, including Ozempic and Wegovy. The regulator warned that semaglutide use has been linked to non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, a condition caused by reduced blood flow to the optic nerve. Patients experiencing sudden sight loss, blurring, or rapidly deteriorating vision are advised to seek immediate medical attention.

stories.headline: Ontario watchdog warns of deficits until 2050 and debt reaching 1.5 trillion dollars
stories.summary: Ontario's Financial Accountability Office released a projection warning that the province faces continuous budget deficits through 2050 and a debt load swelling to $1.5 trillion without significant fiscal correction. The watchdog calculated that the annual deficit will rise from one per cent of gross domestic product to 1.5 per cent by mid-century. Finance Minister Peter Bethlenfalvy's office disputed the long-range economic analysis, defending the government's investment trajectory.

stories.headline: LCBO deploys paid duty police officers across more than 40 high-risk stores
stories.summary: The Liquor Control Board of Ontario has launched Operation Secure Stores, an anti-theft initiative deploying paid duty police officers to more than 40 high-risk retail outlets across the province. The Crown corporation noted that existing loss-prevention measures generated over 2,000 arrests last year, but ongoing brazen robberies targeting premium spirits prompted stricter deterrence. The heightened security presence aims to protect store workers and deter organized theft networks operating in retail centres.

stories.headline: Ford government reviews possible restrictions on out-of-control online gambling ads
stories.summary: Ontario Premier Doug Ford announced that his cabinet is reviewing measures to curtail online gambling advertisements, describing the current volume of ads across the province as out of control. The provincial government faces escalating demands from opposition MPPs and public health advocates to enact comprehensive limits or an outright ban before the end of the year. Ontario was the first Canadian jurisdiction to establish a regulated private market for internet sports betting and gaming in 2022.

stories.headline: Ontario will allow single-occupant vehicles in highway HOV lanes during off-peak hours
stories.summary: The Ontario Ministry of Transportation announced that single-occupancy vehicles will be permitted to travel in high-occupancy vehicle lanes during non-peak hours starting January 1, 2027. Provincial officials stated that opening underutilized lanes will optimize highway capacity and reduce broad traffic congestion, while carpoolers will retain exclusive access during weekday rush hours. Critics and transit advocates have questioned whether diluting HOV restrictions undermines incentives for carpooling and public transit.

stories.headline: Bird advocates and Margaret Atwood press Ottawa to block Pelee Island telecom tower
stories.summary: Author Margaret Atwood and a coalition of conservation groups are calling on the federal government to order a full environmental assessment to halt a proposed 200-metre telecommunications tower on Pelee Island. Opponents argue the planned structure sits directly across a globally recognized migratory corridor for songbirds and poses severe collision hazards. Advocates report gaining substantial public momentum as they lobby federal authorities to intervene before construction proceeds.

stories.headline: Toronto evaluates new revenue measures including a monthly cellphone fee for 911
stories.summary: Toronto city staff have recommended three new municipal revenue tools, led by a proposed $2 monthly fee on mobile phone lines to help fund the city's next-generation 911 system. Facing major budget shortfalls for the upcoming fiscal year, the Executive Committee will consider whether to ask telecommunications carriers to collect the charge, which could generate up to $65.1 million annually. City council must decide how to balance rising emergency service costs against public resistance to added fees.

stories.headline: Federal industry minister pursues talks with Stellantis regarding Brampton auto plant
stories.summary: Federal Industry Minister Mélanie Joly reported holding productive discussions with Stellantis negotiators in Toronto to resolve the future of the automaker's idled assembly facility in Brampton. Talks follow controversy over Stellantis's plans to sell the plant to armoured vehicle manufacturer Roshel, which raised questions about automotive employment and previously pledged government support. Joly expressed confidence that Ottawa and the automaker can find a sustainable path forward to protect manufacturing workers.
